quiz.title: Module 1 — The Foundations of Graphic Design
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers what graphic design is, developing an idea before designing, the principles of design, and how contrast, repetition, movement and white space affect a composition.

questions.prompt: According to the lesson, what is graphic design fundamentally concerned with?
options: Making artwork as visually attractive as possible
Creating decoration for physical and digital spaces
Organising visual elements to communicate a message or idea
Reproducing existing artwork using digital tools
questions.explanation: Graphic design is visual communication — arranging visual elements so they carry a message or idea to an audience, not simply decorating a space.

questions.prompt: What should a designer do before using skills such as layout, colour, and typography to create a design?
options: Choose the most attractive colours available
Develop a solid idea through the design process
Start experimenting with different software tools
Add as many visual elements as possible
questions.explanation: The idea comes before the technique. Layout, colour and typography are the means of expressing an idea, so the idea has to exist first.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the principles of design discussed in the lesson?
options: To provide a framework for understanding how effective designs are created
To ensure that every designer follows exactly the same design style
To teach designers how to use graphic design software
To make every element in a design equally noticeable
questions.explanation: The principles are a framework for thinking about why a design works. They guide decisions rather than dictating one style.

questions.prompt: Which principle helps create a clear difference between elements, making them stand out and improving communication?
options: Repetition
Proportion
Contrast
Movement
questions.explanation: Contrast is difference — light against dark, large against small. It separates elements so the viewer can tell them apart.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of repetition in graphic design, according to the lesson?
options: To make every element visually different
To create consistency and contribute to brand identity
To eliminate the need for hierarchy
To make the design appear more complicated
questions.explanation: Repetition of colours, shapes, type or spacing ties a design together and is what makes a brand recognisable across pieces.

questions.prompt: In the lesson, what does “movement” in design primarily describe?
options: Physical animation within a design
The movement of objects when a design is printed
How the viewer's eyes travel through a design
How quickly a viewer can read the text
questions.explanation: Movement is about directing the eye — the path a viewer follows through the composition as they take it in.

questions.prompt: What does white space refer to in a design?
options: Areas of a design that must always be coloured white
The empty areas surrounding and between design elements
The background colour of a printed design
The space reserved exclusively for typography
questions.explanation: White space is empty space, not necessarily white — it is the breathing room around and between elements.

questions.prompt: Why is controlling white space important in a design?
options: It ensures that every available area is filled with content
It helps fine-tune balance and emphasis within the composition
It makes the design contain more information
It removes the need to use contrast and repetition
questions.explanation: White space is an active design decision. Used well it balances a composition and gives emphasis to what matters.
